# Define the full song list from the note
songs = [
    ("The Ghosts of Our Past", "Mia Sullivan"),
    ("The Fading Light of Memory", "Violet Cascade"),
    ("Painted Skies", "Hazel Winter"),
    ("The Paradox of Our Love", "Oceanic Odyssey"),
    ("The Inescapable Gravity of Love", "Zoe Mitchell"),
    ("Bleeding Sun", "Aria Sterling"),
    ("Trapped in a Daydream", "Nova Harmony"),
    ("Waiting for the Morning Light", "Grace Harrison"),
    ("Vivid Scars", "Lucas Grey"),
    ("Harmony of the Distant Stars", "Lily Moon"),
    ("Fleeting Touch", "Mia Sullivan, Carter Knight"),
    ("Bitter Haze", "Marcus Lane"),
    ("Silent Sorrow", "Aria Sterling"),
    ("The Spiral of Unending Thoughts", "Carter Knight")
]

# We already have song_id for first two, but we'll search all to be safe
# We'll store the song_ids in a dict
song_ids = {}

# Loop through each song, search, and pick the first result that matches title and artist
for title, artist in songs:
    query = f"{title} {artist}"
    result = apis.spotify.search_songs(query=query, access_token=spotify_token, page_limit=5)
    # Find the first result where title matches exactly and artist matches (at least one artist name matches)
    found = None
    for song in result:
        if song['title'].lower() == title.lower():
            # Check if any artist name matches (or if artist string contains the artist name)
            artist_names = [a['name'].lower() for a in song['artists']]
            # For multi-artist songs, we check if all parts of the artist string are present
            artist_parts = [a.strip().lower() for a in artist.split(',')]
            if all(any(part in name for name in artist_names) for part in artist_parts):
